name: Scan libraries job

start.what: the recurring job registration for ScanLibrariesTaskId with the TaskScan cron

actor.who: the system (Hangfire recurring job), on the cron from the TaskScan setting; daily when the setting is invalid
actor.why: registered by ScheduleTasks from the TaskScan server setting; no user starts it

steps.what: the job body: EnqueueScanLibraries(false) decides whether to queue the scan now or later
steps.code: public async Task EnqueueScanLibraries(bool force = false)

steps.what: reads the scan jobs Hangfire holds (enqueued, scheduled, processing)

end.detail: Hangfire job storage (ScanJobQueue.Read: monitoring API reads of enqueued, scheduled and processing jobs)

steps.what: queues ScannerService.ScanLibraries(force) on the scan queue
when the scanner is busy, schedules EnqueueScanLibraries(force) again 3 hours later
tells admins in the UI that the scan was delayed

end.detail: SignalR 'Info' message with code scan-libraries-delayed (EventHub.SendMessageAsync, admins only)

links.to: EnqueueScanLibraries again in 3 hours (this job body)
ActivityStoreService.ingest handles the Info event and adds an activity entry

notes: Registered in TaskScheduler.ScheduleTasks (line 159), called at startup (StartupTasksHostedService.cs:20) and again after the scan schedule setting changes (SettingsService.cs:494). Line 168 registers the same job with Cron.Daily when the TaskScan setting is not a valid cron; line 175 registers it with the converted cron of the setting.

The registered method is EnqueueScanLibraries(false) (line 522); it does not scan itself. The scan is a separate Hangfire job, ScannerService.ScanLibraries (ScannerService.cs:564, queue 'scan'), so it is a runs-later link and its body is not walked here.

In-memory guards not made steps: jobs.FindWaiting(ScanTarget.AllLibraries, force) (line 530, returns early with a log line when a scan of every library is already waiting) and jobs.IsScannerBusy() (line 536); both are extensions in ScanJobExtensions.cs over the snapshot read at 529. Both early returns are plain 'return;', not exits.
The code between lines 527 and 543 runs inside lock (ScanRequestLock) so two requests cannot both see an empty queue.
The job has no HTTP exits, checks or request validation; actor is the system on the cron schedule from the TaskScan server setting.
ScanJobQueue.Enqueue/Schedule/Read only wrap Hangfire's BackgroundJob and monitoring API (ScanJobQueue.cs:32, 38, 72), so they are not walked further.
